title: ledger-consume session-verdict batch
description: The session-verdict file contract run-ledger-consume.mjs's --verdicts flag reads (Wave LEDGER-ZERO, 2026-09-04, operator ruling 'stop offering API when you have a free option with Haiku'). One file = one batch produced by a session lane running FIRST_FETCH_HAIKU_SYSTEM_PROMPT (src/lib/llm/first-fetch-classify.ts, exported verbatim) offline against candidates listed by `--export-candidates`. This file is enforced by run-ledger-consume.mjs's own validateVerdictsFile (pure JS, no schema-engine dependency — see that file's header for why) — this JSON Schema is the human/tooling-readable statement of the SAME contract, not a second hand-typed copy: README.md documents how the two are kept in agreement.

batch.description: This batch's own identifier, e.g. 'ledger-verdicts-001' — matches the filename stem by convention (ledger-verdicts-001.json) but is not itself parsed from the filename.

generated_at.description: When this batch file was written (ISO 8601).

prompt_version.description: Batch-level default: FIRST_FETCH_CLASSIFY_PROMPT_VERSION (src/lib/llm/first-fetch-classify.ts) at the time this batch was classified. Every entry also carries its own prompt_version (entries can, in principle, span a prompt edit mid-batch); the driver validates each entry's own value, this field is documentation of the common case.

classified_by.description: Batch-level default classifier label. 'session-haiku' is currently the only sanctioned value (operator ruling 2026-09-04: use the free session-Haiku path, not the metered API) — a session lane running an actual Haiku model call against FIRST_FETCH_HAIKU_SYSTEM_PROMPT + buildFirstFetchClassifyUserMessage's output, never a human guess or a different model, stamps this.

source_export_ref.description: Optional: the --export-candidates output file this batch classified (audit trail from candidate list to verdict batch). Not required — a session lane may have sourced candidates a different way — but should be set when available.

candidate_id.description: portal_link_candidates.id (uuid) for the row this verdict was produced for. The driver matches verdicts to ledger rows by URL (the field the classify injection point actually receives — see run-ledger-consume.mjs's header for why), and cross-checks candidate_id against the matched row's real id, flagging (never silently discarding) a mismatch as per_item[].verdict_candidate_id_mismatch.

url.description: portal_link_candidates.url — the join key run-ledger-consume.mjs actually matches on.

entity_verdict.description: THE entity-gate signal, identical vocabulary to FirstFetchClassifyOutput.entity_verdict (src/lib/llm/first-fetch-classify.ts). 'portal'/'uncertain' are NOT items and are correct, required answers when genuinely uncertain — never guess 'specific_document' to be safe.

item_type.description: Required, but null is a VALID value — null exactly when entity_verdict is not 'specific_document' (the same null-contract first-fetch-classify.ts enforces: an unsure classification is never silently defaulted to a real item_type).

confidence.description: The session classifier's own confidence in entity_verdict, 0 (guessing) to 1 (certain) — an ADDITIONAL signal beyond the classifier's usual output, informational only today (not consumed by the mint chokepoint), carried through to this run's harness-run artifact per_item[].confidence for a future triage/review pass to read.

rationale.description: One or two sentences, same field/purpose as FirstFetchClassifyOutput.rationale.

classified_by.description: Per-entry classifier label; see the batch-level field of the same name.

classified_at.description: When THIS entry was classified (ISO 8601) — batches may span more than one session-lane run.

prompt_version.description: FIRST_FETCH_CLASSIFY_PROMPT_VERSION at classification time. run-ledger-consume.mjs (partitionVerdictsByPromptVersion) excludes an entry whose prompt_version does not match the driver's own live FIRST_FETCH_CLASSIFY_PROMPT_VERSION from use — treated as no-verdict for that URL (skipped, never sent to the API) — and counts it, rather than rejecting the whole batch: a stale prompt is a version mismatch, handled per-entry, never a silently-accepted drift and never a reason to discard an otherwise-valid large batch. Contrast with a STRUCTURAL schema violation (a missing/malformed required field), which DOES fail the whole file (exit 4) — see README.md.

domain.description: Same vocabulary/routing rule as FirstFetchClassifyOutput.domain. REQUIRED (non-null) when entity_verdict='specific_document' — see the conditional rule below.

allOf.description: entity_verdict='specific_document' requires item_type + the fields buildCandidateSeed (src/lib/intake/portal-harvest.ts) needs to build a mint seed. entity_verdict != 'specific_document' leaves them null, mirroring first-fetch-classify.ts's own contract exactly.
